title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Lumina Insurance
next_steps: Send completed SIG export and SOC 2 report link
Provide evidence pack for KMS and penetration testing
Schedule follow-up call to review outstanding SIG items (week of 2026-09-14)
action_items: Maya Chen: Export SIG answers and attach SOC 2 report PDF by 2026-09-11
Diego Alvarez: Prepare short notes on RBAC/SSO integrations and SCIM behavior by 2026-09-12
Rachel Patel: Share Lumina evidence request spreadsheet and data residency requirements by 2026-09-10
summary: Walkthrough of Lumina's SIG/CAIQ questionnaire. Discussed SOC 2/ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit log retention and access, encryption/KMS options, data residency and private deployment patterns. Agreed to share SOC2 report, SIG export and targeted evidence for KMS and pen test. Follow up next week to close remaining items.
topics: Encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/HSM
SIG / CAIQ questionnaire process and evidence requests
questions: Do you provide customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM integration?
What retention windows exist for audit logs and can we restrict access with RBAC?
Can Redwood support a private control plane / VPC deployment?
What evidence do you have for penetration testing and vulnerability management?
header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rachel Patel (Lumina - Head of Security), Tom Becker (Lumina - IT Ops), Aisha Rahman (Lumina - Procurement)
Recording: yes
Call type: SIG/CAIQ walkthrough (security_review)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we want to walk through the SIG and make sure we capture any evidence requests. Um Diego is here from our security team, he'll jump in on the technical stuff.
[00:16] Rachel Patel: Great thanks Maya, appreciate it. We sent over the questionnaire this morning and there are a few high priority items around KMS and data residency.
[00:34] Diego Alvarez: Hi Rachel, Tom, Aisha. Quick note, we typically provide a SIG export which maps answers to the CAIQ, and we can attach our SOC 2 report and penetration test summary.
[00:50] Tom Becker: When you say SOC 2 report, is that full report or just the attestation? Security wants the full report plus the control narratives if possible.
[01:08] Maya Chen: We usually share the SOC 2 Type II attestation and the bridge letter; control narratives are available under NDA, we can pull those if needed.
[01:28] Rachel Patel: Okay, NDA is fine but we need to confirm timeframes, like last audit date and the period covered, that's on question 1.
[01:44] Diego Alvarez: Last audit ended 2026-06-30, coverage is 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. We'll include that in the export.
[02:05] Aisha Rahman: On procurement side, we need to know about data residency. Lumina requires EU data residency for PII in several products. Can Redwood host in eu-west-1 only?
[02:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we have region pins for hosted inference. For stricter controls we also offer Private deployment with a customer VPC and regional control plane. Note: sometimes transcript tools call it Redwood Privatee, but yeah that's the private deployment option.
[02:52] Tom Becker: For the private deployment, is the control plane customer-managed or still Redwood-managed but in our VPC?
[03:06] Diego Alvarez: It's a hybrid: the control plane can be provided as a private managed control plane within your VPC, or we can provide an on-prem package for fully air-gapped setups. Keys: for CMK you can bring your own key via KMS integration or use our managed KMS.
[03:28] Rachel Patel: Can you clarify the CMK option - is there an HSM-backed KMS and do you support AWS KMS customer-managed keys?
[03:44] Diego Alvarez: We support AWS KMS CMKs for our AWS-hosted Private deployments. For Dedicated and Hosted, customers can opt to use their KMS via integration, and for on-prem we support HSMs - we can provide specifics in the evidence bundle.
[04:07] Aisha Rahman: Evidence for KMS config - we need architecture diagrams and key rotation policies.
[04:19] Maya Chen: We'll attach the KMS architecture diagram and our key rotation policy doc.
[04:32] Rachel Patel: Next, audit logs - questions around retention and who has access. We need at least 2 years retention for some logs and ability to restrict view to a subset of roles.
[04:48] Diego Alvarez: Logs are collected centrally; retention is configurable per-customer in Dedicated/Private. Hosted default retention is 12 months but we can extend with add-ons. RBAC is integrated so you can restrict log access to roles. We'll include a sample RBAC matrix.
[05:12] Tom Becker: How granular is RBAC - can we separate read vs export rights for logs and exclude service accounts?
[05:24] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have role-level permissions (viewer, analyst, operator, admin) and you can disable export for viewer roles. Service accounts are scoped separately; we can show that in the SCIM/SAML docs.
[05:46] Rachel Patel: Speaking of SSO: do you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning? Does SAML assertion contain role claims?
[05:58] Maya Chen: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. SAML role claims can map to our RBAC roles - Diego will share a sample SAML mapping file.
[06:14] Diego Alvarez: Also note group sync via SCIM supports group-to-role mapping, and we support JIT provisioning. We'll include a short implementation note in the handoff.
[06:28] Aisha Rahman: On the SIG doc itself, there are several control descriptions about vulnerability management and pen testing. What evidence do you have for that?
[06:42] Diego Alvarez: We run quarterly vulnerability scans and an annual external pen test. The pen test summary and remediation report can be shared under NDA. We also have our CVE tracking and patching cadence doc.
[07:02] Rachel Patel: Can we get the pen test date and scope? Lumina requires web-facing and API endpoints plus escalation procedures.
[07:16] Diego Alvarez: Last external pen test was 2026-04-10, scope included public API and edge services; internal pen test date is 2026-02-02. We'll include the executive summary and remediation status.
[07:34] Tom Becker: For change management, do you have documented change windows and rollback procedures?
[07:44] Maya Chen: Yes, our change control doc includes rollback playbooks and emergency change policy. We'll attach that.
[07:56] Rachel Patel: Encryption in transit - TLS versions, cipher suites? Our risk team wants to see min TLS 1.2 and modern ciphers.
[08:10] Diego Alvarez: We enforce TLS 1.2+ and prefer TLS 1.3 where supported. We'll attach the TLS configuration and cipher suite list.
[08:24] Aisha Rahman: Who holds the keys for backups and snapshots?
[08:30] Diego Alvarez: Backups are encrypted; for customer-managed KMS the customer holds the KMS key. For provider-managed KMS Redwood rotates keys per policy. We'll include backup encryption evidence.
[08:46] Rachel Patel: Data deletion and e-discovery - can you provide timeline for data deletion requests and deletion verification?
[08:58] Maya Chen: We can perform data deletion per contract; typical SLA is 30 days for full purge across backups, with attestation on request. We'll include deletion process and example attestation.
[09:14] Tom Becker: Is there an immutable audit trail for deletion requests? We need proof changes are logged.
[09:22] Diego Alvarez: Yes, deletion requests are logged and an immutable audit trail is produced. The logs themselves can be shipped to your log collector or retained with us depending on deployment.
transcript_continued:
[09:42] Rachel Patel: Ok good. A few SIG items reference supply chain and third parties. What vendor management do you have for sub-processors?
[10:00] Diego Alvarez: We maintain a sub-processor list and perform vendor risk assessments annually. We'll provide the most recent list and our vendor security questionnaire template.
[10:18] Aisha Rahman: There's also a question about single-tenant vs multi-tenant isolation. For dedicated environments, is there physical isolation?
[10:30] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated instances provide tenant isolation at compute level; on-prem or VPC Private gives you full network isolation. We'll include an architecture note describing isolation boundaries.
[10:48] Maya Chen: Quick note: sometimes the transcript spells our product Redwood Dedicated as "Redwood Delicated" - ignore that, but the capability is dedicated GPU pools with reserved capacity.
[11:08] Rachel Patel: Regarding incident response, do you provide runbooks or will we get notification SLA?
[11:18] Diego Alvarez: We have an incident response playbook and notify customers per SLA - initial acknowledgment within 60 minutes for high severity, full post-incident report within 5 business days.
[11:36] Tom Becker: Can we integrate with our pager/slack channel for alerts?
[11:42] Diego Alvarez: Yes, alerting supports webhook integrations, PagerDuty, and Slack. We'll include sample webhook docs.
transcript_final:
[12:00] Aisha Rahman: On procurement: do you support custom contract language around data residency and subprocessor restrictions?
[12:14] Maya Chen: Yes, we have enterprise legal that handles amendments for residency and subprocessor carve-outs. We'll loop in sales legal after the SIG evidence.
[12:28] Rachel Patel: Outstanding SIG items for us: KMS evidence, pen test executive summary, RBAC mapping, SAML sample, log retention proof, data residency confirmation.
[12:40] Maya Chen: Correct - we'll compile an evidence zip and a completed SIG export. Diego will own technical notes and I'll own SOC2 and contract follow-up.
[12:54] Diego Alvarez: I'll add a brief doc on SCIM group mapping and show how to disable export for viewer roles.
[13:06] Maya Chen: Let's recap next steps - Maya to upload SIG export & SOC 2 by Friday 2026-09-11; Diego to prepare RBAC/SCIM notes by Sunday 2026-09-12; Rachel to send final evidence spreadsheet and any additional questions by Thursday 2026-09-10. We'll schedule a short follow-up the week of 2026-09-14 to close remaining items.
[13:34] Rachel Patel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[13:38] Tom Becker: Thanks, appreciate it.
[13:41] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread with attachments.
[57:30] (call ends)
